goal: improve the two least-improved shapes since the competition began, 1x4096 (1.06x) and 1x8192 (1.17x)

candidates.reason: 5.4% slower; _tri_inv_recursive(2048) does not amortize over 8192's 4 panels (trailing heights 6144/4096/2048) the way it does over 16384's 8 panels. rec_inv is an n>=16384 lever.
+0.23% speed for a 72x residual increase, leaving 1.45x margin to tolerance on a shape whose secret-split conditioning is not controlled. Panel GEMMs are only ~16% of the shape and already tf32.
v1 is a measured loss; combining is pointless

38% slower. exp-062 path is 516 ns/row in situ at batch=1 vs cuSOLVER's fused 373 ns/row. Marginal cost of a 2nd matrix is only 167us (2280.9-2113.8), so the pivot chain is the whole cost and does not shrink with batch; batch=1 has nothing to amortize.

gates.pairedgrid_subset: run for v1/v3/v4; all shapes checker-ok, new_fallbacks empty everywhere
gates.pairedgrid_full_15: NOT RUN - program ladder only spends it after a credible subset win

1x4096.finding: single unblocked serial per-row chain; no GEMM exists to demote, so precision and Triton levers are both structurally void here

1x8192.note: the 'stays on cuSOLVER' comment at submission.py:3686 is stale dead code; the n in _LARGE_CFG gate above it wins

superseded_without_running.item: exp 063 plan item 1 - fix the fused chain+inverse correctness bug (inv_err 0.573)
superseded_without_running.reason: that fusion measured 325.9 ns/row and the v2 'panel + fused inverse' 312.3 ns/row, both slower than the v3 kernel already shipped in #912756 at 296 ns/row

next_action: Scope look-ahead / named-barrier overlap in the 128x32 diagonal block kernel as its own experiment. Measured budget: chain ~11us vs parallel phases ~14us of a 37.9us block; concurrent execution approaches max not sum, ~25us/block = ~195 ns/row. Lifts the five enrolled shapes and is the first design that could make batch=1 blocked factorization beat cuSOLVER's 373 ns/row.
